Drive-through pharmacy — one queue, one server

The smallest interesting queueing model: cars arrive, wait in one line, and are served by whichever pharmacist is free.

What to watch for

Nothing moves. Position carries no meaning here — only occupancy. A red cell is a pharmacist serving a car, green is one free, and the line to the left is the queue. This is what a process-view model looks like when the animation is about state rather than travel.

Underneath

This is a real run of a real model, not a recording. The page fetched the trace (79 KB gzipped) and drew it through the same renderer the desktop animation application uses. Download it and open it there to lay it out yourself.

Read the model's source — the simulation is not modified to be animated; capture is a flag on a run.
